newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zapatistas stall on return to Mexico peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Zapatistas stall on return to Mexico peace talks.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-10-18

text.p: Zapatistas in the southern state of Chiapas will not return to peace talks with the Mexican government until official envoys show "seriousness and respect", rebel leader subcomandante Marcos said late on Thursday.
Marcos, wearing his trademark ski-mask and smoking a pipe, told journalists that government peace negotiators had shown disrespect to the mainly-Maya descended rebels.

"They have been racist toward the Zapatistas and treated them like inferior human beings," Marcos said in this colonial city, making a rare apperance outside the Lacandon jungle where the rebels are in hiding from the army.

In a new bid to persuade rebels back to talks, members of the all-party congressional negotiating committee, known as Cocopa, planned to travel to Mexico City on Friday to meet with Interior Ministry officials and presidential aides.

Peace talks between the Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) and the government were called off in September after 18 months of wrangling. Rebels claimed the government was negotiating in bad faith.
Now, attempts to coax the rebels back to the negotiating table are bogged down in discussions on how the peace discussions should be held.
Aside from the demands for envoys to show seriousness and respect toward the rebels, the Zapatistas also want the government to cede to five points.
Marcos said the Zapatistas would not give way on any of the five points, which range from freeing captured rebels to the naming of a mediator with decision-making authority.

"While the government does not concede these minimal five demands, the EZLN will not return to the peace talks," Marcos said. "They (talks) are not going anywhere on the question of fulfilling the agreements on indian rights and culture."
